hints.explanation: Michael Jordan was nicknamed Air Jordan for his hang time on the basketball court.

lines.AIR: Air Jordan is his nickname and his sneaker line.
lines.BASKETBALL: Michael Jordan is a basketball legend.

hints.explanation: The arcade crane game grabs prizes with a claw, and in Toy Story the little green aliens worship "the claw."

lines.ALIEN: Toy Story's three-eyed aliens chant "The claw!"
lines.CRANE: Claw machines are also called crane games.

hints.explanation: Ancient history is the far past, and Ancient Aliens is the famously meme-able series on the History channel.

lines.ALIEN: Ancient Aliens asks whether aliens visited early humans.
lines.HISTORY: Ancient history covers the earliest civilizations.

hints.explanation: Amazon Prime is the shopping membership, and a prime number divides only by 1 and itself.
Wonder Woman, Diana, is an Amazon princess, and Diana was also the famous Princess of Wales.

lines.AMAZON: Wonder Woman's name is Diana, and she is an Amazon.
lines.PRINCESS: Princess Diana was the beloved Princess of Wales.

hints.explanation: In Snow White, the queen disguised as an old witch gives her a poisoned apple.

lines.APPLE: Snow White bites the witch's apple.
lines.POISON: The witch's apple is laced with poison.

hints.explanation: A limb is an arm or a leg, and a tree's big branches are called limbs too.

lines.BRANCH: A tree's large branches are its limbs, as in going out on a limb.

hints.explanation: The famous statue Venus de Milo is missing both arms, and Venus is the second planet from the Sun.

lines.ARM: The ancient Venus de Milo statue has no arms.
lines.PLANET: Venus is the hottest planet in the solar system.

hints.explanation: The kookaburra is an Australian bird whose call sounds like loud laughter.

lines.LAUGH: The kookaburra's call sounds like laughing.

hints.explanation: Oscar the Grouch lives in a trash can, and the Oscar is Hollywood's top award.

lines.AWARD: The Oscar is the famous film award.
lines.TRASH: Oscar the Grouch lives in a trash can on Sesame Street.

hints.explanation: Your spine runs down your back, and a book's spine holds its pages together.

lines.BACK: The spine runs along your back.
lines.BOOK: A book's spine shows its title on the shelf.

hints.explanation: A pouch is a small bag, and a mother kangaroo carries her joey in one.

lines.BAG: A pouch is a small bag or sack.
lines.KANGAROO: Kangaroo mothers carry their babies in a pouch.

hints.explanation: A golf caddy carries the player's bag, and a tea caddy is a tin for storing tea.

lines.BAG: Golf caddies carry the bag around the course.
lines.TEA: A tea caddy is a container for loose tea.

hints.explanation: In Cast Away, Tom Hanks is stranded on an island with a volleyball he names Wilson, after the sports-ball brand.

lines.BALL: Wilson is a big maker of balls for sports.
lines.ISLAND: Chuck Noland is stranded on a desert island in Cast Away.

hints.explanation: Dodge sells the Ram pickup truck, and dodgeball is the gym-class game.

lines.BALL: Dodgeball is all about dodging the ball.
lines.RAM: Ram trucks were long sold as the Dodge Ram.

hints.explanation: The yellow Minions are obsessed with bananas, and a minion is a lowly helper who serves a boss.

lines.BANANA: In Despicable Me the Minions go wild for bananas.
lines.BOSS: A minion is a follower who does the boss's bidding.

hints.explanation: Donkey Kong collects bananas in the Nintendo games, and King Kong battles Godzilla in the movies.

lines.BANANA: Donkey Kong is famous for collecting and guarding bananas.
lines.GODZILLA: Godzilla vs. Kong pits the two giant monsters against each other.

hints.explanation: An oasis is a green spot of water in the desert, and Oasis is the British band behind "Wonderwall."

lines.BAND: Oasis sang "Wonderwall" and "Don't Look Back in Anger."
lines.DESERT: An oasis is a desert watering hole.

hints.explanation: A journey is a long trip, and Journey is the rock band behind "Don't Stop Believin'".

lines.BAND: Journey is the band that sang "Don't Stop Believin'".
lines.TRIP: A journey is another word for a trip.

hints.explanation: Sheldon Cooper is the genius of The Big Bang Theory, and his childhood is told in the spin-off Young Sheldon.

lines.BANG: Sheldon is the star physicist of The Big Bang Theory.
lines.YOUNG: Young Sheldon shows Sheldon Cooper as a boy genius in Texas.

hints.explanation: Cheers was the classic sitcom set in a Boston bar, and people say cheers when they raise a toast.

lines.BAR: Cheers is the sitcom set in a bar where everybody knows your name.
lines.TOAST: People say cheers when making a toast.

hints.explanation: Barbenheimer was the 2023 double feature of Barbie and Oppenheimer, the film about the atomic bomb.

lines.BARBIE: Barbie was half of the Barbenheimer craze.
lines.BOMB: Oppenheimer tells the story of the atomic bomb.

hints.explanation: Dogs bark and bite, and someone's "bark is worse than their bite."

lines.BITE: Dogs can bite, and the saying says their bark is worse.

hints.explanation: Peanuts is the comic strip starring Charlie Brown, and "buy me some peanuts" is from the baseball song.

lines.BASEBALL: "Take Me Out to the Ball Game" asks for peanuts and Cracker Jack.
lines.COMIC: Peanuts is the classic comic strip with Charlie Brown and Snoopy.

hints.explanation: Diamond is the hardest natural mineral, and a baseball infield is called the diamond.

lines.BASEBALL: The baseball infield is known as the diamond.

hints.explanation: Water goes down the sink drain, and in basketball slang to drain a shot is to sink it.

lines.BASKETBALL: Basketball players drain shots from long range.
lines.SINK: A sink empties through its drain.

hints.explanation: To charge an enemy is to assault it, and assault and battery is a pair of criminal charges.

lines.BATTERY: In law, battery is the partner of assault.
lines.CHARGE: A charge is an assault on the enemy, and assault is also a legal charge.

hints.explanation: In basketball a jumper is a jump shot, and jumper cables bring a dead car battery back to life.

lines.BATTERY: Jumper cables connect a dead battery to a working one.
lines.SHOT: A jumper is basketball slang for a jump shot.

hints.explanation: Sting was the lead singer of The Police, and bees sting.

lines.BEE: A bee's sting is its defense.
lines.POLICE: Sting fronted The Police ("Every Breath You Take").

hints.explanation: The Statue of Liberty holds a torch high, and the cracked Liberty Bell is in Philadelphia.

lines.BELL: The Liberty Bell is famous for its crack.
lines.TORCH: Lady Liberty raises her torch over New York Harbor.

hints.explanation: The asteroid belt lies between Mars and Jupiter, and an asteroid impact is the leading explanation for the dinosaurs' extinction.

lines.BELT: Most asteroids orbit in the asteroid belt.
lines.DINOSAUR: An asteroid strike helped wipe out the dinosaurs 66 million years ago.

hints.explanation: Benjamin Button is the man who ages backwards, and "Benjamins" is slang for hundred-dollar bills with Ben Franklin on them.

lines.BILL: The $100 bill shows Benjamin Franklin, so the bills are nicknamed Benjamins.
lines.BUTTON: The Curious Case of Benjamin Button follows a man who ages in reverse.

hints.explanation: At a restaurant you ask for the check, meaning the bill, and in chess "check" means the king is under attack.

lines.BILL: The check is the bill at a restaurant.
lines.CHESS: Check, and then checkmate, in chess.

hints.explanation: Tweety is the little yellow cartoon bird who lives in a birdcage while Sylvester the cat schemes to get in.

lines.CAGE: Tweety's home is a birdcage that Sylvester keeps trying to raid.

hints.explanation: Florence Nightingale was a famous nurse, and the nightingale is a songbird.

lines.BIRD: The nightingale is a songbird known for singing at night.

hints.explanation: Jack Frost is said to nip at your nose in winter, and a nip is a small bite.

lines.BITE: A nip is a quick little bite.
lines.FROST: Jack Frost nips at noses on cold days.

hints.explanation: Veins carry blood back to the heart, and miners follow a vein of gold through rock.

lines.BLOOD: Veins carry blood back to your heart.
lines.GOLD: A vein of gold is a seam of ore running through rock.

hints.explanation: During a total lunar eclipse, the moon turns red and is called a blood moon.

lines.BLOOD: A blood moon happens during an eclipse.
lines.MOON: A lunar eclipse darkens the moon.

hints.explanation: Navy SEALs are elite U.S. Navy forces, and navy is a dark shade of blue.

lines.BLUE: Navy blue is a deep, dark blue.
lines.SEAL: SEAL teams are the Navy's special forces.

hints.explanation: Monopoly is a classic board game, and in business a monopoly is a company with no rivals.

lines.BOARD: Monopoly is one of the best-known board games.
lines.BUSINESS: A business monopoly controls a whole market.

hints.explanation: Tug-of-war is played with a rope, and a tugboat pulls big ships into port.

lines.BOAT: Tugboats tow ships in and out of harbor.
lines.ROPE: In tug-of-war two teams pull a rope.

hints.explanation: Lightning strikes as a bolt, and in the classic films a lightning storm brings Frankenstein's monster to life.

lines.BOLT: A single flash of lightning is called a bolt.
lines.FRANKENSTEIN: In the movies, Dr. Frankenstein harnesses lightning to animate his creature.

hints.explanation: Harry Potter has a lightning-bolt scar, and Scar is the villainous lion in The Lion King.

lines.BOLT: Harry Potter's forehead scar is shaped like a lightning bolt.
lines.LION: Scar is Simba's wicked uncle in The Lion King.

hints.explanation: A short circuit can blow a fuse, and cartoon bombs have a lit fuse (and someone with a short fuse is quick to anger).

lines.BOMB: Cartoon bombs sizzle along a fuse before going boom.
lines.SHORT: A short circuit trips or blows a fuse.

hints.explanation: A genie grants wishes, and a genie in a bottle is the classic image (and a Christina Aguilera hit).

lines.BOTTLE: A genie lives in a bottle or lamp.
lines.WISH: Genies grant three wishes in stories.

hints.explanation: In myth Pandora opened the box that released the world's troubles, and Pandora is the jewelry brand famous for bracelet charms.

lines.BOX: Pandora's box let all the evils into the world.
lines.CHARM: Pandora bracelets are built from collectible charms.

hints.explanation: In The Wizard of Oz, the Scarecrow wants a brain and the Tin Man wants a heart.

lines.BRAIN: The Scarecrow goes to Oz to ask for a brain.
lines.HEART: The Tin Man goes to Oz to ask for a heart.

hints.explanation: You pop a bubble, and Pop is a nickname for Dad.

lines.FATHER: Pop is a familiar name for a father.

hints.explanation: A coach is a long-distance bus, and the gym teacher is often called Coach.

lines.BUS: A coach is another word for a bus.
lines.GYM: Gym teachers are often called Coach.

hints.explanation: Jelly Belly is the jelly bean brand, and your belly button sits in the middle of your belly.

lines.BUTTON: Your belly button is your navel.
lines.JELLY: Jelly Belly makes famous gourmet jelly beans.

hints.explanation: Shutters cover a window, and a camera's shutter opens to take a photo.

lines.CAMERA: A camera clicks when its shutter opens and closes.
lines.WINDOW: Window shutters block light and storms.

hints.explanation: Glamping is glamorous camping, with luxury comforts like real beds in the tent.

lines.CAMP: Glamping is a fancy way to camp.
lines.LUXURY: Glamping brings luxury to the outdoors.

hints.explanation: Mars is the Red Planet, and Mars is the company behind candy like M&M's and Snickers.

lines.CANDY: Mars is a big candy maker.
lines.RED: Mars is known as the Red Planet.

hints.explanation: Two sweets share the word: fluffy cotton candy at the fair and striped candy canes at Christmas.

lines.CANE: Candy canes are striped peppermint hooks hung on Christmas trees.
lines.COTTON: Cotton candy is spun sugar that looks like fluffy cotton.

hints.explanation: A cannonball is fired from a cannon, and pool is played with balls on a table.

lines.POOL: Pool players knock balls into pockets.

hints.explanation: Yankee Doodle stuck a feather in his cap, and the Yankees are New York's famous baseball team.

lines.CAP: "Yankee Doodle went to town... stuck a feather in his cap."
lines.NEW YORK: The New York Yankees are baseball's most famous team.

hints.explanation: A broken bone may need a cast, and actors heading on stage are told to break a leg.

lines.CAST: A bad break can leave you in a cast.
lines.STAGE: Break a leg is the good-luck wish before going on stage.

hints.explanation: Tom Thumb is the tiny hero of the old fairy tale, and Tom is the cat in Tom and Jerry (a male cat is also called a tomcat).

lines.CAT: Tom is the cat forever chasing Jerry, and a tomcat is a male cat.
lines.THUMB: Tom Thumb is a fairy tale boy no bigger than his father's thumb.

hints.explanation: Sesame Street is the famous kids' show, and Open Sesame opens the cave in Ali Baba.

lines.CAVE: Open Sesame unlocks the thieves' cave.
lines.STREET: Sesame Street is the classic children's show.

hints.explanation: Chain mail is armor made from linked metal rings.

lines.CHAIN: Chain mail is made of linked metal chain rings.
lines.MAIL: Mail is the old name for this kind of armor.

hints.explanation: Goldilocks breaks Baby Bear's little chair, and the "Goldilocks zone" is the not-too-hot, not-too-cold region where a planet could hold liquid water.

lines.CHAIR: Goldilocks sits in Baby Bear's chair and breaks it.
lines.PLANET: Astronomers search the Goldilocks zone for life-friendly planets.

hints.explanation: A gauntlet is an armored glove, and throwing one down issues a challenge.

lines.CHALLENGE: To throw down the gauntlet is to issue a challenge.
lines.GLOVE: A gauntlet is a heavy protective glove.

hints.explanation: Hurdles are a track event, and a hurdle is any challenge to get over.

lines.CHALLENGE: A hurdle is a challenge to overcome.
lines.TRACK: Runners jump hurdles on the track.

hints.explanation: In classic comics and films, Clark Kent ducks into a phone booth to change into Superman.

lines.CHANGE: Clark Kent makes a quick change into his Superman costume.
lines.PHONE: The phone booth is Superman's classic changing room.

hints.explanation: Checkmate ends a chess game, and mate is slang for a friend.

lines.CHECK: Check becomes checkmate when the king cannot escape.
lines.FRIEND: In Britain and Australia, a mate is a friend.

hints.explanation: To mold something is to shape it, and blue cheese gets its veins from mold.

lines.CHEESE: Blue cheese is made with mold on purpose.
lines.SHAPE: You can mold clay into any shape.

hints.explanation: Baby chicks say "peep," and Little Bo Peep lost her sheep.

lines.CHICK: A chick's tiny call is a peep, as in Easter Peeps.
lines.SHEEP: Little Bo Peep has lost her sheep.

hints.explanation: Mars was the Roman god of war, and Mars is also the candy company behind the Mars bar.

lines.CHOCOLATE: The Mars bar is a chocolate candy bar.
lines.WAR: Mars is the Roman god of war, and the red planet is named after him.

hints.explanation: Jack Skellington, the Pumpkin King of Halloween Town, tries to take over Christmas in The Nightmare Before Christmas.

lines.CHRISTMAS: Jack kidnaps Santa and tries to run Christmas himself.
lines.HALLOWEEN: Jack rules Halloween Town as the Pumpkin King.

hints.explanation: Ebenezer Scrooge is the rich miser of A Christmas Carol.
Skin is the body's largest organ, and a pipe organ fills a church with music.

lines.CHURCH: Many churches have a big pipe organ.
lines.SKIN: Skin is the largest organ of the human body.

hints.explanation: Pi relates a circle's circumference to its diameter, and Pi Day is celebrated on March 14.

lines.CIRCLE: Pi is the ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter.
lines.MARCH: March 14 (3/14) is celebrated as Pi Day.

hints.explanation: P. T. Barnum billed his circus as the Greatest Show on Earth.

lines.CIRCUS: Barnum built a famous traveling circus.
lines.SHOW: The Greatest Show on Earth was Barnum's slogan.

hints.explanation: In Peter Pan the crocodile that ate Captain Hook's hand also swallowed a ticking clock.

lines.CLOCK: You can hear the crocodile coming by the tick-tock of the clock inside it.
lines.HOOK: The crocodile hunts Captain Hook for the rest of his hand.

hints.explanation: Cuckoos are famous for laying eggs in other birds' nests, and a cuckoo clock has a little bird pop out to call the hour.

lines.CLOCK: A cuckoo clock's bird pops out on the hour.

lines.CLOCK: An hourglass is a simple sand clock.

lines.CLOSET: A wardrobe closet is the doorway to Narnia.

lines.CLOWN: The Joker is Batman's clown-faced enemy.
lines.WILD: "Jokers wild" means the joker can stand for any card.

hints.explanation: An iron is a type of golf club, and Iron Man is Marvel's armored hero.

lines.CLUB: Golfers carry irons as well as woods and a putter.

hints.explanation: Pocahontas sings Colors of the Wind in the Disney film.

lines.COLOR: Pocahontas sings about all the colors of the wind.
lines.WIND: Colors of the Wind is the song from Pocahontas.

hints.explanation: A comic strip is drawn in panels, and a group of judges is also called a panel.

lines.COMIC: Each box in a comic strip is a panel.

hints.explanation: In The Polar Express, a train conductor punches the children's tickets on the way to the North Pole.

lines.CONDUCTOR: The Polar Express has a famous train conductor.
lines.POLAR: The Polar Express is the Christmas train story.

lines.COOKIE: Fig Newtons are soft cookies filled with fig paste.
lines.FORCE: Force is measured in newtons, named after Isaac Newton.

hints.explanation: A potato is a vegetable, and a couch potato is someone who lounges on the sofa all day.

lines.COUCH: A couch potato spends hours on the couch.
lines.VEGETABLE: The potato is a starchy vegetable.

hints.explanation: Dolly Parton is a country music legend, and Dolly was the famous cloned sheep.

lines.COUNTRY: Dolly Parton is a country music star.
lines.SHEEP: Dolly the sheep was the first mammal cloned from an adult cell.

hints.explanation: Frasier Crane is the psychiatrist who hosts a call-in radio show in the sitcom Frasier.

lines.CRANE: Dr. Frasier Crane gives his surname to this word.
lines.RADIO: Frasier hosts a radio advice show in Seattle.

lines.CRASH: Rebooting is the classic fix after a crash.

hints.explanation: Wimbledon is tennis played on grass, where fans eat strawberries and cream.

lines.CREAM: Strawberries and cream are the Wimbledon snack.

hints.explanation: Strawberries and cream are the traditional treat at Wimbledon, the famous tennis tournament.

lines.CREAM: Fans at Wimbledon eat strawberries and cream.
lines.TENNIS: Wimbledon is the oldest tennis championship.

hints.explanation: Pinocchio sings "I've Got No Strings," and Jiminy Cricket acts as his conscience.

lines.STRING: The wooden puppet boasts he has no strings to hold him down.

hints.explanation: Cricket is played with a flat bat, and a vampire bat drinks blood.

lines.VAMPIRE: Some vampires in stories turn into bats, and vampire bats are real.

hints.explanation: An X is a cross shape, and on pirate maps X marks the spot where the treasure is buried.

lines.CROSS: An X is a cross, as in kisses or a crossed-out answer.

hints.explanation: The rook is the chess piece shaped like a castle tower, and a rook is also a bird in the crow family.

lines.CROW: Rooks are black birds closely related to crows.
lines.TOWER: The rook chess piece looks like a little tower.

hints.explanation: One full rotation of the Earth on its axis makes roughly one day.

lines.DAY: A day is about one rotation of the Earth.
lines.EARTH: Earth spins on its axis about once a day.

hints.explanation: You shuffle a deck of cards, and shuffle mode plays your songs in random order.

lines.DECK: Shuffling mixes a deck of cards.
lines.SONG: Shuffle plays your songs in a random order.

hints.explanation: A pentagon is a five-sided shape, and the Pentagon is the headquarters of the U.S. Department of Defense.

lines.DEFENSE: The Pentagon houses the Department of Defense.
lines.SHAPE: A pentagon is a five-sided shape.

hints.explanation: Dessert is usually the last course of a meal, and golf is played on a course.

lines.DESSERT: Dessert is usually the final course.
lines.GOLF: Golf is played on a golf course.

hints.explanation: High tide is when the sea comes furthest in, and Tide is a best-selling laundry detergent.

lines.HIGH: The ocean rises to high tide roughly twice a day.

hints.explanation: Surfers keep an eye on the tide, and Tide is a famous laundry detergent.

lines.DETERGENT: Tide is a big laundry detergent brand.
lines.SURFING: Surfers check the tide before paddling out.

hints.explanation: A genius is brilliant, and a brilliant is a sparkling style of diamond cut.

lines.DIAMOND: The round brilliant is the classic diamond cut.
lines.GENIUS: A genius has a brilliant mind.

hints.explanation: Lucy in the Sky with Diamonds is a Beatles song.

lines.DIAMOND: Lucy has diamonds in the song title too.
lines.SKY: Lucy is in the sky in the Beatles song.

hints.explanation: Abbott and Costello's comedy routine is "Who's on First?", and Doctor Who is the time-traveling TV hero.

lines.DOCTOR: Doctor Who travels through time in the TARDIS.
lines.FIRST: "Who's on First?" is a classic baseball comedy sketch.

hints.explanation: To shrink is to get smaller, and "shrink" is slang for a psychiatrist.

lines.DOCTOR: A shrink is a nickname for a psychiatrist or therapist.

hints.explanation: A laser pointer projects a red dot, and a pointer is a hunting dog that points at game.

lines.DOG: Pointers are hunting dogs bred to point toward birds.
lines.LASER: Cats famously chase the dot from a laser pointer.

hints.explanation: Goose down fills pillows and jackets, and "Duck, Duck, Goose" is the playground circle game.

lines.DOWN: Goose down is a famously warm, soft feather filling.
lines.DUCK: In Duck, Duck, Goose, the picker taps heads saying "duck" until shouting "goose!"

hints.explanation: In one of film's most famous images, Marilyn Monroe's white dress billows up as a subway train passes beneath the grate she stands on.

lines.DRESS: Marilyn Monroe's white halter dress from The Seven Year Itch is iconic.
lines.SUBWAY: The breeze that lifts her dress comes from a subway train below the grate.

hints.explanation: A drill sergeant trains new soldiers.

lines.DRILL: A drill sergeant runs boot-camp drills.
lines.SOLDIER: A sergeant is a soldier's rank.

hints.explanation: Morning dew forms tiny drops on the grass, and Mountain Dew is a bright green soda.

hints.explanation: Partygoers dance in a conga line, and a conga is a tall Afro-Cuban drum.

hints.explanation: An eagle is a bird, and in golf an eagle beats a birdie by one stroke.

lines.EAR: Spock's pointy ears are his signature look.

hints.explanation: The White House holds an Easter Egg Roll, and an egg roll is a crispy snack.

lines.EASTER: Easter eggs are hunted every spring.

lines.EGYPT: The Great Sphinx of Giza guards Egypt's pyramids.
lines.PUZZLE: The riddle of the Sphinx is one of the oldest puzzles in stories.

hints.explanation: Omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet, a symbol for the end, and Omega is a famous watch brand.

lines.END: Alpha and omega means the beginning and the end.

hints.explanation: Spotted Dalmatians are the famous firehouse dogs that ride on fire engines.

lines.ENGINE: Dalmatians are the traditional mascots of fire engines.
lines.SPOT: Dalmatians are known for their black spots.

hints.explanation: A clock has a face and hands.

lines.FACE: The front of a clock is its face.
lines.HAND: The hands point to the time.

hints.explanation: Tinker Bell is Peter Pan's fairy, named because she mends pots and kettles like a tinker.

lines.FAIRY: Tinker Bell is the most famous fairy in Neverland.
lines.PAN: Tinker Bell is Peter Pan's loyal companion.

lines.STICK: Hockey players pass the puck with their sticks.

hints.explanation: Kids put a lost tooth under their pillow for the tooth fairy.

lines.FAIRY: The tooth fairy visits while you sleep on your pillow.
lines.TOOTH: A lost tooth goes under the pillow.

hints.explanation: Fans in a packed stadium stand up in turn to make the wave.

lines.WAVE: Crowds do the wave around a stadium.

lines.MEXICO: Coco follows Miguel through a Mexican Day of the Dead.

hints.explanation: A feather boa is a fluffy scarf, and a boa is a large snake that squeezes its prey.

lines.FIREWORKS: The Fourth of July is celebrated with fireworks.

lines.FLY: The fly is the unwanted guest.
lines.SOUP: The soup is the scene of the crime.

lines.FRANCE: The Statue of Liberty was a gift from France.
lines.STATUE: Lady Liberty is the famous statue in New York Harbor.

hints.explanation: To frost a cake is to ice it, and icing is a hockey call for shooting the puck the length of the ice.

lines.FROST: Frost a cake and you have added icing.
lines.HOCKEY: Icing is a common hockey call.

hints.explanation: The tomato is botanically a fruit but is usually cooked and served as a vegetable.

lines.FRUIT: Botanically, a tomato is a fruit.
lines.VEGETABLE: Tomatoes are treated as vegetables in the kitchen.

hints.explanation: After a big meal you feel stuffed, and the Thanksgiving turkey is often stuffed too.

lines.TURKEY: A stuffed turkey is the Thanksgiving centerpiece.

hints.explanation: David killed the giant Goliath with a single stone from his sling.

lines.GIANT: Goliath was the giant David defeated.
lines.STONE: David's weapon was a stone and a sling.

hints.explanation: David Bowie's Space Oddity opens with "Ground Control to Major Tom."

lines.GROUND: Ground Control is the mission control voice in the song.
lines.MAJOR: Major Tom is the astronaut drifting into space.

hints.explanation: Ground chuck is ground beef, and a woodchuck (another name for a groundhog) stars in the tongue twister about how much wood it could chuck.

lines.GROUND: Ground chuck is a common cut of ground beef.
lines.WOOD: "How much wood would a woodchuck chuck?"

hints.explanation: In the Bible, Samson was super strong until his hair was cut.

lines.HAIR: Samson's strength was tied to his uncut hair.

hints.explanation: In politics, hawks push for war and doves push for peace, and the dove is the classic peace symbol.

lines.HAWK: A hawk is the opposite of a dove in politics.
lines.PEACE: The dove is a symbol of peace.

hints.explanation: The organ is a musical instrument, and the heart is an organ of the body.

lines.HEART: The heart is a vital organ.
lines.INSTRUMENT: The organ is a big keyboard instrument.

hints.explanation: A stiletto is a thin, high heel, and also a slim dagger.

lines.HEEL: Stilettos are shoes with tall, thin heels.
lines.KNIFE: A stiletto is a narrow-bladed knife.

hints.explanation: Alice falls down the rabbit hole into Wonderland, and later steps through the looking-glass, a mirror.

lines.HOLE: Alice tumbles down a rabbit hole.
lines.MIRROR: In Through the Looking-Glass she climbs through a mirror.

hints.explanation: Hook, line, and sinker are the parts of a fishing rig, and the phrase means believing something completely.

lines.HOOK: Hook, line, and sinker go together.
lines.LINE: A sinker weighs down the fishing line.

hints.explanation: James Brown was called the Godfather of Soul, and The Godfather film has the famous scene with a horse's head in a bed.

lines.HORSE: In The Godfather, a film producer wakes to find a horse's head in his bed.
lines.SOUL: James Brown is known as the Godfather of Soul.

hints.explanation: A bullseye is the center of a target, and Bullseye is Woody's horse in Toy Story.

lines.HORSE: Bullseye is the horse in Toy Story.
lines.TARGET: The bullseye is the middle of a target.

hints.explanation: Tony Stark is Iron Man, and the Starks of Game of Thrones warn that winter is coming.

lines.WINTER: The Starks' motto is Winter Is Coming.

hints.explanation: In Britain a car's trunk is called the boot, and Italy is shaped like a boot.

lines.TRUNK: The British word for a car trunk is the boot.

hints.explanation: Jam and pickles both come in jars, and being in a jam or in a pickle both mean being in trouble.

lines.PICKLE: Pickles are sold in jars too.

hints.explanation: The emperor penguin is the largest penguin, and Japan is the last country with a reigning emperor.

lines.JAPAN: Japan's monarch holds the title Emperor.
lines.PENGUIN: Emperor penguins are the biggest penguins.

hints.explanation: A jelly doughnut has a jelly filling, and a dentist puts a filling in a tooth with a cavity.

lines.JELLY: Jelly is a classic doughnut filling.
lines.TOOTH: A filling repairs a cavity in a tooth.

hints.explanation: A bank vault is a giant safe, and to vault is to jump, as in the pole vault.

lines.JUMP: Pole vaulters jump over a high bar using a pole.
lines.SAFE: A vault is a walk-in safe for valuables.

hints.explanation: Spaghetti is a long noodle, and Lady and the Tramp share a famous spaghetti kiss.

lines.KISS: The spaghetti kiss is the iconic scene from Lady and the Tramp.

hints.explanation: A kiwi fruit has fuzzy brown skin, and the fuzz is old slang for the police.

lines.KIWI: Kiwi fruit is covered in fuzz.
lines.POLICE: The fuzz is slang for the police.

hints.explanation: Garfield is the lazy orange comic-strip cat who hates Mondays.

lines.ORANGE: Garfield is an orange tabby cat.

hints.explanation: A capital is a big uppercase letter, and each state has a capital city.

lines.LETTER: Capital letters are the uppercase ones.
lines.STATE: Every state has a capital city.

hints.explanation: Every magnet has a north and a south pole, and Santa lives at the North Pole.

lines.SANTA: Santa's home is the North Pole.

hints.explanation: Patrick Star is SpongeBob's starfish best friend, and St. Patrick's Day falls in March.

lines.STAR: Patrick Star is SpongeBob's starfish buddy.

hints.explanation: In Mario games, Koopa Troopas are turtles whose shells you can kick and throw.

lines.MARIO: Koopa Troopas are classic Mario enemies.
lines.SHELL: A Koopa's shell becomes a weapon when kicked.

hints.explanation: The Phantom of the Opera hides in the theater and wears a half mask.

lines.MASK: The Phantom wears a famous white mask.
lines.THEATER: The Phantom haunts the Paris opera theater.

hints.explanation: Hobbits live in Middle-earth, and the hobbit Bilbo finds the One Ring.

lines.RING: Bilbo the hobbit finds the One Ring.

hints.explanation: Do-re-mi is a major scale, and a major is a military officer's rank.

lines.MILITARY: Major is an officer rank in the military.
lines.SCALE: Major and minor are the two main kinds of musical scale.

hints.explanation: Colonel Sanders guarded KFC's secret recipe, and a colonel is a military rank.

lines.MILITARY: A colonel is a senior military officer.
lines.SECRET: KFC's Colonel kept a secret blend of herbs and spices.

hints.explanation: Thin Mints are the best-known Girl Scout cookie, chocolate-coated with a mint flavor.

lines.MINT: Mint gives Girl Scout Thin Mints their cool flavor.
lines.THIN: Thin Mints are a famous Girl Scout cookie.

hints.explanation: In legend werewolves change under the full moon and can be stopped by silver.

lines.MOON: Werewolves transform under the full moon.
lines.SILVER: A silver bullet is the classic werewolf weakness.

hints.explanation: George Washington's face is carved into Mount Rushmore.

lines.MOUNTAIN: Mount Rushmore is a mountain in South Dakota.
lines.WASHINGTON: Washington is one of the four faces on Rushmore.

hints.explanation: A hammer is meant to hit the nail, but a missed swing can hit your thumb instead.

lines.NAIL: A hammer drives nails into wood.
lines.THUMB: A missed hammer swing on your thumb is a classic cartoon ouch.

hints.explanation: Apple makes the Apple Watch, and New York is nicknamed the Big Apple.

lines.NEW YORK: New York City is the Big Apple.
lines.WATCH: The Apple Watch is Apple's smartwatch.

hints.explanation: Shredder is the ninja villain of the Ninja Turtles, and a paper shredder cuts documents to strips.

lines.NINJA: Shredder leads the Foot Clan of ninjas.

hints.explanation: Popeye the Sailor Man loves Olive Oyl and always has a pipe in his mouth.

lines.PIPE: Popeye chomps on a corncob pipe.

hints.explanation: Dumbledore leads the Order of the Phoenix and keeps a pet phoenix named Fawkes.

lines.ORDER: Dumbledore founded the Order of the Phoenix to fight Voldemort.
lines.PHOENIX: Fawkes, Dumbledore's phoenix, bursts into flame and is reborn.

hints.explanation: The Louvre in Paris has a glass pyramid entrance and the most famous painting in the world, the Mona Lisa.

lines.PAINTING: The Mona Lisa hangs in the Louvre.
lines.PYRAMID: The Louvre's glass pyramid is its iconic entrance.

hints.explanation: Sails were traditionally made of canvas, and painters work on stretched canvas.

lines.PAINTING: Many paintings are made on canvas.
lines.SAIL: Canvas is the classic sail cloth.

hints.explanation: On the bridge of Khazad-dum, Gandalf slams down his staff and shouts "You shall not pass!"

lines.PASS: "You shall not pass!" is Gandalf's famous line.
lines.STAFF: Gandalf the wizard carries a wooden staff.

hints.explanation: Ivory is a classic floating soap, and piano keys are nicknamed ivories.

lines.SOAP: Ivory soap is famous for floating.

hints.explanation: A frame holds a picture, and to frame a suspect is to make them look guilty.

lines.PICTURE: A picture sits in a frame.
lines.SUSPECT: Framing a suspect means planting false evidence.

hints.explanation: Pink Floyd's famous rock album is The Wall.

lines.PINK: Pink Floyd is the band's full name.
lines.WALL: "Another Brick in the Wall" is from The Wall.

hints.explanation: A right hook is a punch, and Captain Hook is the pirate villain of Peter Pan.

lines.PIRATE: Captain Hook is the most famous pirate in Neverland.
lines.RIGHT: A right hook is a classic boxing punch.

hints.explanation: Bugs munch on plants, and spies plant bugs to listen in on secret talks.

lines.SPY: A spy's bug is a hidden microphone.

hints.explanation: A square root is a math idea, and roots anchor a plant in the soil.

lines.PLANT: Plants draw water through their roots.
lines.SQUARE: Every number has a square root.

hints.explanation: Hamlet is Shakespeare's famous play, and a hamlet is a very small town.

lines.PLAY: Hamlet is one of Shakespeare's best-known plays.
lines.TOWN: A hamlet is a tiny village or town.

hints.explanation: Punch is the classic seaside puppet of Punch and Judy, and a sock pulled over your hand makes a sock puppet.

lines.PUNCH: Punch and Judy is a traditional puppet show.
lines.SOCK: A sock puppet is the simplest homemade puppet.

hints.explanation: A jigsaw is a picture puzzle, and it is also a power tool for cutting curves.

lines.TOOL: A jigsaw is a saw for cutting curved shapes.

hints.explanation: In the Looney Tunes cartoons, Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck shout "Rabbit season!" "Duck season!" at the hunter Elmer Fudd, who is always chasing that rabbit.

lines.RABBIT: Elmer Fudd is forever hunting Bugs Bunny, the wascally wabbit.
lines.SEASON: Bugs and Daffy argue over whether it is rabbit season or duck season.

hints.explanation: In the fable, the slow tortoise wins the race against the hare.

lines.RACE: The tortoise beats the hare in the race.
lines.SLOW: The tortoise is slow and steady.

hints.explanation: The Olympic torch travels in a relay, and a relay race passes a baton between runners.

lines.RACE: A relay race is run in legs by a team.
lines.TORCH: The Olympic torch is carried in a relay before the Games.

hints.explanation: A computer monitor is a screen, and a monitor lizard is a large reptile.

lines.REPTILE: Monitor lizards, like the Komodo dragon, are reptiles.
lines.SCREEN: A monitor is a computer screen.

hints.explanation: The Avengers are Marvel's famous superhero team, and to avenge something is to take revenge for it.

lines.REVENGE: Avenging a wrong means taking revenge for it.
lines.TEAM: The Avengers are Earth's mightiest superhero team.

hints.explanation: The Roomba is a robot vacuum that cleans floors on its own.

lines.ROBOT: A Roomba is a little floor-cleaning robot.
lines.VACUUM: A Roomba is a vacuum cleaner.

hints.explanation: A lasso is a cowboy's looped rope, and Ted Lasso is the TV coach who takes over an English soccer team.

lines.ROPE: A lasso is a rope with a sliding loop.
lines.SOCCER: Ted Lasso coaches AFC Richmond in the hit soccer comedy.

hints.explanation: King Arthur's knights met at the Round Table.

lines.ROUND: Arthur's table was round so no knight sat at the head.
lines.TABLE: King Arthur gathered his knights at the Round Table.

hints.explanation: A comet has a glowing tail, and Comet is one of Santa's reindeer.

lines.SANTA: Comet pulls Santa's sleigh with Dasher and Dancer.
lines.TAIL: Comets grow bright tails near the Sun.

hints.explanation: Cupid is the arrow-shooting symbol of Valentine's Day, and Cupid is one of Santa's reindeer.

lines.SANTA: Cupid pulls Santa's sleigh with the other reindeer.
lines.VALENTINE: Cupid is the symbol of Valentine's Day.

hints.explanation: Dorothy is swept to Oz by a tornado and meets the Scarecrow on the yellow brick road.

lines.SCARECROW: The Scarecrow joins Dorothy to ask the Wizard for a brain.
lines.TORNADO: A Kansas tornado carries Dorothy's house to Oz.

hints.explanation: A tempest is a violent storm, and The Tempest is a Shakespeare play that begins with a shipwreck.

lines.SHAKESPEARE: The Tempest is one of Shakespeare's last plays.
lines.STORM: A tempest is a fierce storm.

hints.explanation: Many vaccines are given as a shot, and they train your body to fight off viruses.

lines.SHOT: Most vaccines are given as a shot in the arm.
lines.VIRUS: Vaccines help protect against viruses such as flu and measles.

hints.explanation: Hamlet holds up Yorick's skull ("Alas, poor Yorick!"), and a hamlet is a tiny town.

lines.SKULL: Hamlet's graveyard speech is delivered to a skull.
lines.TOWN: A hamlet is a small village.

hints.explanation: White smoke from the Sistine Chapel signals that a new pope has been chosen.

lines.SMOKE: Smoke rises from the chapel when the vote ends.
lines.WHITE: White smoke means a new pope.

hints.explanation: In Greek myth Medusa has snakes for hair and turns anyone who looks at her to stone.

lines.SNAKE: Medusa's hair is a nest of living snakes.
lines.STONE: Medusa's gaze turns people to stone.

hints.explanation: Olaf is Frozen's friendly snowman who dreams of summer.

lines.SNOWMAN: Olaf is the snowman Elsa brings to life.
lines.SUMMER: Olaf sings "In Summer," not knowing what heat does to snow.

hints.explanation: A zookeeper looks after the animals, and a goalkeeper guards the net in soccer.

lines.SOCCER: A goalkeeper is the keeper in soccer.
lines.ZOO: A zookeeper cares for zoo animals.

hints.explanation: Captain America: The Winter Soldier is a Marvel film, and a captain is a military officer.

lines.WINTER: The Winter Soldier faces Captain America.

hints.explanation: Sonic means relating to sound, and Sonic the Hedgehog is a famous video game hero.

lines.SOUND: A sonic boom is a blast of sound.
lines.VIDEO GAME: Sonic the Hedgehog is a classic video game.

hints.explanation: Plankton is SpongeBob's tiny villain who schemes for the Krabby Patty formula, and many whales feed on plankton.

lines.SPONGEBOB: Plankton plots against SpongeBob and Mr. Krabs.
lines.WHALE: Blue whales eat tiny plankton and krill.

hints.explanation: Three strikes in a row in bowling is called a turkey, and turkey is the Thanksgiving main course.

lines.STRIKE: Three strikes in a row is a turkey.
lines.THANKSGIVING: Turkey is the star of Thanksgiving dinner.

hints.explanation: London's subway is nicknamed the Tube, and TV is sometimes called "the tube."

lines.SUBWAY: The London Underground is known as the Tube.
lines.TELEVISION: Old TVs had picture tubes, so TV is "the tube."

hints.explanation: Spades are a suit in a deck of cards, and a spade is a digging tool.

lines.SUIT: Spades is one of the four card suits.
lines.TOOL: A spade is a garden tool like a shovel.

hints.explanation: The corona is the Sun's glowing outer atmosphere, and coronaviruses are named for their crown-like spikes.

lines.SUN: The Sun's corona is visible during a total eclipse.
lines.VIRUS: Coronaviruses look like they wear a crown, corona in Latin.

hints.explanation: In Greek myth, Icarus flew too close to the sun and the wax on his wings melted.

lines.WING: Icarus flew on wings of feathers and wax.

hints.explanation: Too many sweets can give you a cavity in a tooth.

lines.TOOTH: A cavity is a hole in a tooth.

hints.explanation: Leonardo DiCaprio starred in Titanic, and Leonardo is the blue-masked leader of the Ninja Turtles.

lines.TURTLE: Leonardo leads the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles.

hints.explanation: A pick is a digging tool, and a toothpick cleans between your teeth.

lines.TOOL: A pick is a classic digging tool.
lines.TOOTH: A toothpick is a little pick for your teeth.

hints.explanation: Crews drill a well to reach water or oil, and a dentist drills a tooth before filling it.

lines.TOOTH: The dentist's drill is the sound everyone dreads.
lines.WELL: A drill bores a well deep into the ground.

hints.explanation: You answer to the boss at work, and a video game level often ends with a boss fight.

lines.VIDEO GAME: A boss is the big enemy at the end of a game level.
lines.WORK: The boss runs things at work.
